constructors-and-object-state.label: Constructors and Object State
constructors-and-object-state.summary: Use `__init__` to create per-object state, distinguish instance state from class-level state, and keep mutable lists separate between objects.

mc-constructors-and-object-state-storing.title: Class state or instance state?
mc-constructors-and-object-state-storing.prompt: Which statements correctly distinguish class variables from instance variables? Choose all that apply.
mc-constructors-and-object-state-storing.hint: Values on `self` belong to one object; values such as `Car.wheels` live at the class level.

help.concept: Instance variables are stored on one object through `self`. Class variables are defined in the class body.
help.hint_1: Look for `self.` when identifying per-object state.
help.hint_2: A class-level value can be read from the class itself.

options.a: `self.make` can differ from one `Car` object to another.
options.c: Every value assigned on `self` is shared by all `Car` objects.
options.d: A class variable is recreated separately inside every object.

sketch-0.title: Use __init__ to establish instance state
sketch-0.bodyMarkdown:
A constructor gives each new object its starting instance state.

```python
class Movie:
    def __init__(self, title, year):
        self.title = title
        self.year = year

film = Movie("Arrival", 2016)
```

`self.title` and `self.year` belong to that particular Movie instance.

A second Movie can start with different values while using the same constructor.

sketch-1.title: Separate class-level values from per-object values
sketch-1.bodyMarkdown:
Class state belongs to the class; instance state can differ from object to object.

```python
class Bicycle:
    wheels = 2

    def __init__(self, color):
        self.color = color

blue_bike = Bicycle("blue")
red_bike = Bicycle("red")
```

Both bicycles share `wheels == 2`, but each object owns its own `color`.

Use class attributes for genuinely shared facts, not values that should vary per instance.

sketch-2.title: Create mutable state separately for each object
sketch-2.bodyMarkdown:
Mutable instance state should be created separately for each object.

```python
class Notebook:
    def __init__(self, owner):
        self.owner = owner
        self.tags = []

first = Notebook("Ari")
second = Notebook("Noor")

first.tags.append("school")
```

`second.tags` is still empty because every constructor call created a fresh list.

This pattern prevents unrelated objects from accidentally sharing mutable state.
